citation: Examining the challenges posed to parents by the contemporary screen environments of children: a qualitative investigation (PMC)
'Everything kind of revolves around technology': a qualitative exploration of families' screen use experiences (PMC)
mechanisms: Screen time is a necessary tool for future readiness, not just leisure, because children must not be disadvantaged in a technological world where screen viewing is the norm.
Screen time is a risk to be managed through strict parental control, because excessive use causes observable harm like addiction, headaches, and reduced social skills.
Not all screen time is equal, because TV is social and homework is purposeful, while tablets and games are isolating and addictive.
Screen time guidelines must accommodate parental need for respite, because screens are a necessary coping tool when parents face practical constraints and need to maintain sanity.
Screen time interventions should foster self-regulation rather than impose external limits, because children must learn their own boundaries to develop autonomy.
objection_patterns: Will this make my child fall behind in a technological world?
Is this going to cause addiction or health problems?
Is this screen social and educational, or isolating and addictive?
Does this give me a break when I need to get things done?
Will this help my child learn to manage their own time?
